authenticatedStartingCi.reuse: These downloaded authentic receipts certify the starting source, never the new changes. No duplicate workflow was launched.

canonicalMemo.scope: Required existing TenantModelScope, with matching actual caller and scope owner before the optional memo catch. Existing canonical reservation, price version and settlement preserved, purpose complexity, maximum output 700 tokens.
canonicalMemo.account: Existing platform Zhipu account, unchanged. Zhipu BYOK is not in the canonical admitted credential-provider list. The test does not invent such an account or claim its custody is verified. Unselected revoked/rotated user rows cannot retarget the platform request. Supported OpenRouter BYOK rotation/revocation remains covered at the actual shared call sites.
canonicalMemo.securityFailure: Model policy and stale issued-attempt denials propagate instead of being converted into an optional null memo. Ordinary provider/accounting availability failure can still skip the optional memo. Raw provider error bodies no longer reach the memo log.

upstreamProjectData.demonstratedGap: Legacy local memory and session history use per-user _local/_workspace namespaces. Those namespaces contain no database project identity and cannot establish that old cached context belongs to the selected project.
upstreamProjectData.correction: Use the existing stores with an admitted-project/repository namespace. No new table, cache, identity issuer or accounting system. Check current projects.id/user_id/github_repo_name before server history or hydration, and carry that expected repository through the existing model scope and actual SoftwareAgent/build calls for final dispatch revalidation. Preserve owner/repository/branch validation and defensive clones in the existing receivers.
upstreamProjectData.legacyRecovery: Never guess a project's identity from legacy local cache. Keep ambiguous legacy data intact. An update/resume requesting unavailable old context fails with an actionable reload message. An explicit new build can start without inheriting legacy files. Explicit client-provided local input remains untrusted user data. GitHub-backed projects can reload their selected authorized remote source when the new namespace misses.
upstreamProjectData.githubProof: Actual hydration uses canonical GitHub credential consumption and the provider's repository/ref/tree response before reusing an owner/project namespace with matching head and paths. Foreign selected repository fails before credential/provider dispatch. GitHub denial cannot fall through to cached or browser source.
limitations: Controlled Supabase/GitHub protocol fixtures, not live RLS or GitHub verification
Client-supplied text is untrusted input, not independently certified ownership
Logical non-database workspaces retain the original owner-scoped contract
No complete in-flight GitHub credential revocation or all generic model callers certification

uploadReview.provedScope: Actual exported legacy GitHub mirror writer and actual Storage SDK: original issued context, owner-prefixed paths, public/unknown/unavailable bucket refusal, exact retry path, closed production migration window and safe logging. Existing private-bucket admission is reused.
uploadReview.remaining: Legacy writer has no found production importer, but exported/future reachability is not erased. This test does not certify encrypted writer payloads, every user-provider mirror producer, a bucket privacy change during upload, live Storage policies, or arbitrary uploads. Keep all three records open.

previewReview.provedScope: Actual shared resolver used by HTTP and both WebSocket branches, real SDK serialization against controlled DB protocols. Signed grant, persisted owner/project/session, lifetime, declared HTTP port and validated internal target. Forged subject/parent/session, revoked/expired/malformed grants and unsafe targets fail before a target connection.
previewReview.remaining: No actual HTTP/WebSocket target traffic is claimed. Payload/header classification and forwarding, stream lifetime/revocation and exact tenant runtime selection remain transport obligations. HTTP currently copies non-hop-by-hop incoming headers, so platform/app credential separation still needs actual caller/transport proof. Do not certify both sockets from the resolver test.
